prompt.adult: When Jesus saw the crowds, where did He go up before He sat down to teach?
prompt.child: Jesus saw big crowds. Where did He go up and sit down to teach?
prompt.teen: When Jesus saw the crowds, where did He go up to teach?
prompt.older: According to Matthew 5:1, where did Jesus go up when He saw the multitudes?

verses.text: And seeing the multitudes, He went up on a mountain, and when He was seated His disciples came to Him.

explanation.adult: Matthew 5:1 tells where Jesus went. Read the words after "He went up."
explanation.child: Read Matthew 5:1. Find "He went up." The next words tell where.
explanation.teen: Check Matthew 5:1. Where He went comes right after "He went up."
explanation.older: Matthew 5:1 names the place right after "He went up on."

teaching.extended_explanation: Matthew 5:1 says Jesus saw the crowds, went up, sat down, and His disciples came to Him there.
teaching.takeaway: Jesus went up on a mountain to teach.

prompt.adult: Jesus said the pure in heart are blessed. What did He say they will do?
prompt.child: Jesus said people with pure hearts are blessed. What did He promise they will do?
prompt.teen: Jesus said the pure in heart are blessed. What will they do?
prompt.older: According to Matthew 5:8, what is promised to the pure in heart?

verses.text: Blessed are the pure in heart, For they shall see God.

explanation.adult: Matthew 5:8 gives the promise after the word "For." Read the second half of the verse.
explanation.child: Read Matthew 5:8. After "For they shall," the verse gives the promise.
explanation.teen: Check Matthew 5:8. The promise follows "For they shall."
explanation.older: Matthew 5:8 states the promise in its second line, after "For they shall."

teaching.extended_explanation: Each blessing in Matthew 5 names a kind of person and then gives a promise. Read the promise for the pure in heart.
teaching.takeaway: The pure in heart shall see God.

prompt.adult: Jesus said the peacemakers are blessed. What did He say they will be called?
prompt.child: Jesus said people who make peace are blessed. What will they be called?
prompt.teen: Jesus said peacemakers are blessed. What will they be called?
prompt.older: According to Matthew 5:9, what shall the peacemakers be called?

verses.text: Blessed are the peacemakers, For they shall be called sons of God.

explanation.adult: Matthew 5:9 gives the promise to the peacemakers. Read the words after "called."
explanation.child: Read Matthew 5:9. Find the word "called." The words after it are the answer.
explanation.teen: Check Matthew 5:9. The name they are given comes after "called."
explanation.older: Matthew 5:9 states what peacemakers will be called at the end of the verse.

teaching.extended_explanation: Matthew 5:9 has two lines. The first names the peacemakers. The second tells what they will be called.
teaching.takeaway: The peacemakers shall be called sons of God.

prompt.adult: Jesus compared His followers to something that can lose its flavor. What was it?
prompt.child: Jesus said His followers are like something that gives food flavor. What was it?
prompt.teen: Jesus compared His followers to something that can lose its flavor. What?
prompt.older: According to Matthew 5:13, Jesus' hearers are compared to what, which can lose its flavor?

verses.text: “You are the salt of the earth; but if the salt loses its flavor, how shall it be seasoned? It is then good for nothing but to be thrown out and trampled underfoot by men.

explanation.adult: Matthew 5:13 begins with Jesus telling His listeners what they are. Read the first sentence.
explanation.child: Read Matthew 5:13. The first words tell what Jesus says His followers are.
explanation.teen: Check Matthew 5:13. The first sentence says what they are "of the earth."
explanation.older: Matthew 5:13 opens with the comparison, then asks what happens if it loses its flavor.

teaching.extended_explanation: In Matthew 5:13, Jesus names something people use to season food and warns about it losing its flavor.
teaching.takeaway: Jesus said His followers are the salt of the earth.

prompt.adult: What did Jesus say cannot be hidden?
prompt.child: Jesus said one thing cannot be hidden. What was it?
prompt.teen: Jesus mentioned something that cannot be hidden. What was it?
prompt.older: According to Matthew 5:14, what did Jesus say cannot be hidden?

verses.text: “You are the light of the world. A city that is set on a hill cannot be hidden.

explanation.adult: Matthew 5:14 has two sentences. Read the second one.
explanation.child: Read Matthew 5:14. The second sentence names something that cannot be hidden.
explanation.teen: Check Matthew 5:14. The second sentence gives the answer.
explanation.older: Matthew 5:14 gives the example in its second sentence.

teaching.extended_explanation: Jesus called His followers the light of the world, then gave an example of something everyone can see from far away.
teaching.takeaway: A city that is set on a hill cannot be hidden.

prompt.adult: Jesus told His followers to let their light shine before others. Why?
prompt.child: Jesus said to let your light shine so people can see your good works. What will happen then?
prompt.teen: Why did Jesus say to let your light shine before others?
prompt.older: According to Matthew 5:16, for what reason should believers let their light shine before men?

choices.text: So that they can win every argument they start
So that other people will always be afraid of them
So that they will be paid a large reward
So that others will glorify your Father in heaven

verses.text: Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father in heaven.

explanation.adult: Matthew 5:16 gives the reason after the word "that." Read what people will do when they see good works.
explanation.child: Read Matthew 5:16. After people see your good works, the verse tells what they will do.
explanation.teen: Check Matthew 5:16. The reason comes after people see your good works.
explanation.older: Matthew 5:16 states the purpose: what others will do once they see good works.

teaching.extended_explanation: Matthew 5:16 says good works are seen by others, and then tells whom they will honor because of it.
teaching.takeaway: We let our light shine so others will glorify our Father in heaven.

prompt.adult: In the prayer Jesus taught, what do we ask God to give us this day?
prompt.child: In the prayer Jesus taught, we ask God to give us something today. What is it?
prompt.teen: In the prayer Jesus taught, what do we ask God to give us today?
prompt.older: According to Matthew 6:11, what does the prayer ask God to give us this day?

verses.text: Give us this day our daily bread.

explanation.adult: Matthew 6:11 is one short request. Read the last words.
explanation.child: Read Matthew 6:11. It is short. The last words tell what we ask for.
explanation.teen: Check Matthew 6:11. The request ends with what we ask for.
explanation.older: Matthew 6:11 is a single petition; what is requested closes the verse.

teaching.extended_explanation: Matthew 6:11 asks God for what we need for one day at a time.
teaching.takeaway: Jesus taught us to ask God for our daily bread.

prompt.adult: The prayer Jesus taught asks God to forgive us. According to that prayer, whom do we forgive?
prompt.child: Jesus taught His friends how to pray. When we ask God to forgive us, who does the prayer say we forgive?
prompt.teen: In the prayer Jesus taught, we ask God to forgive us. Whom does the prayer say we forgive?
prompt.older: According to Matthew 6:12, whom does the prayer say we forgive?

verses.text: And forgive us our debts, As we forgive our debtors.

explanation.adult: Matthew 6:12 has two lines. Read the second line, which begins with "As we." Look at whom it names.
explanation.child: Read Matthew 6:12. The second line starts with "As we." Read whom it names.
explanation.teen: Check Matthew 6:12. The second line, starting "As we," names whom it speaks of.
explanation.older: Matthew 6:12 completes the request with a line beginning "As we," and names a group there.

teaching.extended_explanation: Matthew 6:12 has two parts: what we ask God to do, and what we do toward others. Read the second line, which begins with “As we.”
teaching.takeaway: We ask God to forgive us as we forgive our debtors.
